newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS - Telmex obtains $1 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Telmex obtains $1 bln loan.

text.p: Mexican telephone giant Telefonos de Mexico said on Friday it had taken out a whopping $1 billion loan to carry out investment plans and increase its leverage.

Analysts said the company, Mexico's largest, appeared to be building a war chest for both taking on its new rivals in Mexico and tapping into telephone markets beyond Mexico's border, especially in the United States.

The one-year credit, syndicated among 30 banks, has an interest rate of LIBOR plus 60 basis points, which analysts said was proof of investors' confidence in Telmex's financial muscle despite having recently lost its long-distance monopoly.
Investors welcomed the news, driving up Telmex's stock price 3/8 to $42 on Wall Street in late trade on Friday.
Company officials said the loan completed Telmex's financing needs for the short-run and said the money would mostly be used to fund the firm's $1-1.1 billion investment plan this year.

"Together with the commercial paper and pagares (notes), we feel satisfied with our level of financing for the moment," Gerardo Munoz, director of investor relations, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Earlier this year, Telmex issued three billion pesos worth of one-year commercial paper and followed up by issuing five billion pesos worth of medium-term "pagares", or notes.
The three moves pushed up the company's debt to capitalization ratio from 13 percent at the end of 1996 to about 25 percent at present, Munoz said.
"Our debt level at the end of last year was at its lowest level since our privatization (in 1990)," Munoz said.
Telmex said earlier this year it planned to raise capital expenditures from $550 million last year to at least $1 billion this year, mostly for improving its network in the face of competition.

Telmex lost its decades-old monopoly in long-distance service last year, and this year has had to begin connecting its rivals, including AT&T and MCI, to its own network and hence to millions of phones.
To offset its market share loss at home, the company has begun looking beyond its borders.

Telmex owner and billionaire Carlos Slim said in January that the firm planned to begin offering long-distance service in the United States by year's end -- mostly aimed at the swelling numbers of Hispanic immigrants.

"(The loan) shows their desire to build out new operations. It appears they are building a war chest so they can not only better take on their rivals but also expand into the U.S. market," Paul Aran, an analyst at James Capel in New York, said.
Aran said Telmex could also be considering buying into cellular operations in Brazil.
"They are not going to go out and blow a billion overnight, but they are clearly interested in other opportunities," he said.
